eli: Ran an nsys/NSight capture on an 8xA100 run where kernel selector flips from wavefront=64 -> wavefront=32 at step ~220.

eli: Observed a cascade: kernel switch -> extra memcpy + small kernels -> NCCL all-reduce queues up -> 100-200ms tail latency spikes. Trace attached.

sara: Can you paste the snippet? wondering if it's the KV prefetch path causing the memcpy.

eli: ```
# from nsight timeline (simplified)
220: kernel_select(wf=64)
221: matmul_k32_wf64
222: kv_prefetch_async(copy: 256KB)
223: kernel_select(wf=32)
224: matmul_k16_wf32
225: ncclAllReduce(...)
# note: memcpy sits on stream 2 blocking the expected compute stream leading to nccl backlog
```

dan: :eyes: That copy size looks suspicious — prefetch chunking was recently changed in batching heuristics PR#482. @matt could that cause the wavefront fallback?

matt: short answer: yes. PR introduced chunk_size heuristic that reduces copy granularity for long sequence tails. It can force a kernel variant with smaller shared memory since we try to fit prefetch buffers. I pushed a perf test but maybe not multi-gpu with simultaneous prefetch.

sara: repro plan:
- reproduce with nsight + nvprof on 8gpus
- instrument kernel_selector.log to emit chosen wf and shared mem usage
- run with old and new chunk_size env to see difference

eli: quick local repro showed that disabling kv_prefetch (env:KV_PREFETCH=0) removes memcpy on hot path and NCCL queues are smooth. Timeline after toggle: tail spikes disappear.

runtime-bot: CI perf run 3742 failed: 2x tail-latency regression on 8-GPU matrix-mul test. Link: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/3742

dan: let's file a minimal regression test and revert the heuristic until we can pick chunk sizes that don't change kernel selection mid-run.

matt: I'll draft a patch to prefer kernel stability over marginal memory win, and add a multi-gpu nsight job to PR checks. ETA today.

eli: cool. dropping the full capture into build:3742 artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/3742/nsight/trace.sq

sara: thanks — I'll take the nsight slice and try a flame graph to see where memcpys align with allreduce starts.

eli: ack, will follow up with a short perf note once we confirm.
